attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: Hadamard-semigroup and boundary-OPE factorization gap: Yang-Mills estimates do not yet prove multiplicative nonzero \(B\), vanishing additive contacts, or infinite divisibility of the quotient.
steps: Fixed-collar reflection positivity and RG convergence give a PSD collar-limit matrix \(\widehat N\) by the closed-cone argument.
Boundary OPE analysis is inserted only at collar collapse: if it is multiplicative, \(\widehat N=\widehat B\circ\widehat M\), so the intended target is \(\widehat M=\widehat N\oslash\widehat B\).
Therefore same-theory OS positivity is exactly finite PSD of the quotient on realized Wilson blocks; pairwise damping is necessary but not sufficient.
If collar quotients form a continuous Hadamard semigroup, Schoenberg converts the all-minors test to log-CND; without that structure, determinants remain the valid tests.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The finite matrix reduction is formal once the boundary data exist, but the analytic construction of those data for reflected Wilson hairpins is missing.

assumptions: Fixed-collar RG convergence is valid for every reflected finite Wilson block.
The boundary OPE gives an entrywise nonzero multiplicative factor \(B\) after diagonal normalization.
Additive contacts vanish, e.g. positivity plus zero diagonal, or are already included in the locked target.
The realized Wilson core is closed under the finite collar probes used in the quotient test.
definitions: source object: finite reflected Wilson collar OS matrices \(N_\delta=(S_\delta(\Theta F_i^\delta,F_j^\delta))\) with \(N_\delta\ge0\).
target object: continuum OS matrices \(M=(S(\Theta F_i,F_j))\) on the locked gauge-invariant Wilson/local algebra.
controlled interface: regulated reflection-positive Schwinger forms -> OS-positive continuum Schwinger functions via the quotient \(M=N\oslash B\).
same-theory condition: collar removal uses the predeclared Wilson renormalization and embeddings; no boundary counterterm, algebra enlargement, or pair-dependent redefinition is allowed.

equations.label: boundary quotient factorization
equations.latex: \widehat N_{ij}=\widehat B_{ij}\widehat M_{ij},\qquad \widehat M=\widehat N\oslash\widehat B
equations.valid_when: The boundary anomaly is purely multiplicative, entries of \(\widehat B\) are nonzero, and additive contacts have been eliminated.

equations.label: exact finite OS test
equations.latex: \widehat M\ge0\Longleftrightarrow \sum_{i,j}\overline c_i c_j\,{\widehat N_{ij}\over \widehat B_{ij}}\ge0\quad\forall c
equations.valid_when: The finite Wilson family belongs to the locked same-theory test algebra; this is the exact valid criterion, not a heuristic.

equations.label: semigroup certificate
equations.latex: q_t=e^{-t h},\ q_{s+t}=q_s\circ q_t,\ q_t\ge0\ \forall t\ge0\Longleftrightarrow \sum_{i,j}\overline z_i z_j h_{ij}\le0\ (\sum_i z_i=0)
equations.valid_when: Only for a continuous normalized Hermitian Hadamard semigroup; it is not valid evidence from one quotient matrix alone.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A principal minor of \(\widehat N\oslash\widehat B\) is negative for a realized Wilson block; the first likely falsifier is a three-hairpin determinant.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Reduces reflection-plane collar collapse to a finite Schur-preimage problem, while isolating log-CND as an optional certificate requiring extra semigroup structure.
candidate_lemmas.statement: For each finite locked Wilson collar family, after diagonal normalization and removal of additive contacts, same-theory OS positivity is equivalent to PSD of \(\widehat Q=\widehat N\oslash\widehat B\). If \(Q_t\) is a valid Hadamard semigroup, log-CND is a sufficient all-minors certificate.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot if boundary OPE shows nonmultiplicative contacts or a negative quotient determinant for a locked Wilson triple.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote if a dense Wilson core has vanishing additive contacts, multiplicative nonzero \(B\), and PSD quotients, or a valid semigroup with log-CND generator.
control_decision.reason: The branch now has a sharp finite obstruction and a conditional certificate; both are mathematically testable on Wilson hairpin blocks.

dependency_updates.description: Closed-cone passage covers fixed collars; reflection-plane collapse is now a finite Schur-preimage condition.
The Wilson core must include collar probes and preserve renormalization across the boundary trace.
Topology must control fixed-collar OS forms plus boundary OPE limits defining \(B\) and quotient minors.

falsifiers: falsifier: a realized three-hairpin Wilson block has \(\det(\widehat N\oslash\widehat B)<0\) although every 2-by-2 quotient minor is nonnegative.
falsifier: the boundary OPE contains a nonpositive additive contact with zero diagonal, so the entrywise multiplicative quotient model is invalid.
falsifier: collar quotients fail \(q_{s+t}=q_s\circ q_t\); then log-CND is not a valid certificate, only direct finite minors remain.
falsifier: reflection-plane removal forces a new cusp or boundary counterterm outside the locked gauge-invariant algebra, violating same-theory.
branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 211 separates the exact bridge from a tempting overclaim: OS positivity after Wilson collar collapse is finite PSD of \(\widehat N\oslash\widehat B\). Log-CND is useful only if a valid Hadamard semigroup is proved. The next real work is boundary OPE computation, not topology naming.
branch_outputs.next_experiment: Compute the boundary OPE for three reflected Wilson hairpins with common footprint; extract \(\widehat B\), form \(\widehat N\oslash\widehat B\), and test the 3-by-3 determinant before invoking any semigroup certificate.
